p:cNvPr.descr: PART 2: An image depicting oxidation of a polyunsaturated fatty acid. The image begins with linoleoyl-CoA cis-delta9, cis-delta12, which begins with a red 18, which bonds up and right, then down and right two times, then bonds up and right, then double bonds right (second line is red) to 12 (red), then binds down and right then up and right, then double bonds (second line is red) right to 9 (red). It then bonds down and right then up and right four times to C with a red number one to the left of it. A wavy blue line cross the down and right bonding lines. C double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down, identified as b oxidation (three cycles). Another arrow jets off this arrow to the right to 3 acetyl-CoA. Next is cis-delta3, cis-delta6, which begins with 12 (red) and bonds up and right to down and right two times, then bonds up and right. It then double bonds right to 6 (red). The second double bond line is red. It then bonds down and right to 5 (red), then up and right to 4 (red). It then double bonds right (second line is red) to 3 (beta) in red, then bonds down and right to 2 (alpha) in red. It then bonds up and right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. Below this are reversible lines, identified as delta3, delta2-enoyl-CoA isomerase (in blue). Below this is trans-delta2, cis-delta6. This begins with 12 (red) and is the same as the one above up to the red 5, then bonds up and right to 4 (red), then bonds down and right to 3 (beta) in red, then double bonds up and right to 2 (alpha) in red. Then double bonds down and right to C, which double bonds down and right to O and up and right to S-CoA. below this is a black arrow pointing down, represented as beta oxidation cycle (one cycle, and first oxidation of second cycle). On the right side of the arrow, another arrow jets off, pointing to acetyl-CoA. Below this, trans-delta2, cis-delta4 begins with 10 (red), then bonds up and right, then down and right two times. It then bonds up and right to 5 (red), then double bonds right (second line is red) to 4 (red), then bonds down and right to 3 (red). It then double bonds up and right (second bond line is red) to 2 (red), then bonds down and right to C. C has a red 1 above it. C bonds up and right to S-CoA and double bonds down and right to O. Below this is an arrow pointing down, identified as 2,4-dienoyl-CoA reductase (in blue). To the right of the arrow is a curved arrow pointing from NADPH [plus] H+ to NADP+. Below this is trans-delta3. It begins with 10 (red), then bonds up and right, then down and right two times, then bonds up and right to 5 (red), then down and right to 4 (red), then double bonds up and right to 3 (second bond line is red), then down and right to 2 (red), then up to C (red 1 is superscripted to the left of C). C double bonds up and right to O and down and right to S-CoA. Below this is an arrow pointing down, identified as enoyl-CoA isomerase (in blue). Below this is trans-delta2, which is the same as trans-delta3, but has no 5, and instead of double bonding between 4 and 3, it double bonds between 3 and 2. Below this, is an arrow pointing down, identified as beta oxidation (four cycles). This arrow points to 5 acetyl-CoA.
